people.name: Nelson Mandela
people.description: South African anti-apartheid revolutionary who spent 27 years in prison. Became South Africa's first Black president and promoted national reconciliation.

people.name: Mahatma Gandhi
people.description: Led India's nonviolent independence movement against British colonial rule. Pioneered civil disobedience and peaceful resistance tactics.

people.name: Martin Luther King Jr.
people.description: American civil rights leader who organized peaceful protests against racial segregation. His advocacy led to the Civil Rights Act of 1964.

people.name: Malala Yousafzai
people.description: Pakistani activist shot by the Taliban for advocating girls' education. Became the youngest Nobel Peace Prize laureate.

people.name: Eleanor Roosevelt
people.description: Chaired the UN committee that drafted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948). Advocated for civil rights and women's rights.

people.name: Frederick Douglass
people.description: Escaped enslaved person who became America's most influential abolitionist. His writings provided firsthand testimony of slavery's cruelty.

people.name: Harriet Tubman
people.description: Escaped slavery and returned to the South approximately 13 times to guide others to freedom via the Underground Railroad.

people.name: Cesar Chavez
people.description: Co-founded the United Farm Workers union and organized strikes and boycotts to improve conditions for agricultural laborers.

people.name: Sojourner Truth
people.description: Escaped slavery and became a powerful advocate for abolition and women's suffrage. Her 'Ain't I a Woman?' speech challenged both racial and gender discrimination.

people.name: Desmond Tutu
people.description: South African Anglican bishop who opposed apartheid and later chaired the Truth and Reconciliation Commission. Won the Nobel Peace Prize.

people.name: Susan B. Anthony
people.description: Key figure in the American women's suffrage movement. Co-founded the National Woman Suffrage Association and campaigned for women's right to vote.

people.name: Abraham Lincoln
people.description: U.S. president who issued the Emancipation Proclamation and pushed for the 13th Amendment to abolish slavery.

people.name: Muhammad Yunus
people.description: Created microcredit/microfinance through Grameen Bank, providing loans to impoverished people without collateral. Nobel Peace Prize winner.

people.name: Olympe de Gouges
people.description: Authored Declaration of the Rights of Woman during French Revolution, demanding women's inclusion in universal rights.

people.name: Wangari Maathai
people.description: Founded Green Belt Movement, empowering women to plant trees while linking environment to democracy. First African woman Nobel Peace Prize winner.

people.name: Greta Thunberg
people.description: Started global youth climate movement through school strikes, demanding emergency action on climate crisis.
